punchline: Many adults still read exactly the way they learned as small children.
thirty_sec: In Limitless, Jim Kwik argues most people never update the reading habits they learned as kids. He points to subvocalization, silently saying every word, and regression, needlessly jumping back to reread. His main tool is a visual pacer: a finger or pen moving under the line. Reading researchers caution that big speed gains often cost comprehension, so match speed to the material and check understanding.
question: How often do your eyes jump back to reread when you don't really need to?
